item.text:
**Reused evidence**
None. No prior chapter evidence applied cleanly as reusable 7B evidence for Sheikh Hasina in 2022.

**New evidence**
- Public housing commitment and delivery.
  SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"No one to stay homeless in Bangladesh, PM declares after providing homes to about 33,000 destitute families","publisher":"UNB News","publication_date":"2022-04-26","url":"https://unb.com.bd/category/Bangladesh/no-one-to-stay-homeless-in-bangladesh-pm-declares-after-providing-homes-to-about-33000-destitute-families/91837","claim":"Hasina said the government would keep building houses for homeless people, that no one would remain landless or shelter-less, and that the Ashrayan project had just handed homes to 32,904 families.","locator":"L183-L186 and L214-L221","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Direct contemporaneous report of a public speech with concrete beneficiary counts and explicit policy intent.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly in 2022 and directly about social-policy intent and delivery.","ruler_attribution":"Strongly attributable to Sheikh Hasina as prime minister and project sponsor, though it remains a self-presented commitment rather than an independent audit.","contrary_evidence":["Later evidence shows her family also benefited from secret plot allocations in 2022, which complicates the integrity picture."],"lenses":["7B.8","7B.10"]}

- Public pledge of inclusion and responsibility to all citizens.
  SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Govt will ensure home for all: PM","publisher":"Jago News","publication_date":"2022-07-21","url":"https://www.jagonews24.com/en/national/news/62865","claim":"Hasina said the government would provide houses to the homeless irrespective of political affiliation and views, and described herself as responsible to every citizen of Bangladesh.","locator":"L33-L40 and L52-L55","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Direct contemporaneous report of a public statement with specific inclusion language and delivery context, though still self-presented.","final_evidence_use":"context","period_fit":"Directly in 2022 and directly about public ethical positioning and inclusivity.","ruler_attribution":"Attributed to Hasina personally as a public promise, but not independently verified as practice in the article.","contrary_evidence":["Secret plot-allocation evidence from 2022 suggests a more patronage-prone side of the same governing network."],"lenses":["7B.8","7B.10"]}

- Response to transparency criticism over vaccination spending.
  SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"No one to stay homeless in Bangladesh, PM declares after providing homes to about 33,000 destitute families","publisher":"UNB News","publication_date":"2022-04-26","url":"https://unb.com.bd/category/Bangladesh/no-one-to-stay-homeless-in-bangladesh-pm-declares-after-providing-homes-to-about-33000-destitute-families/91837","claim":"In response to criticism that Covid vaccination spending lacked transparency, Hasina said all vaccination costs should be counted and that the government vaccinated people free of cost.","locator":"L208-L211","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Contemporaneous report of Hasina’s own response to a transparency criticism, but it is self-justifying and not an independent reconciliation of the accounts.","final_evidence_use":"context","period_fit":"Directly in 2022 and directly about scrutiny of government accounting.","ruler_attribution":"Hasina personally addressed the criticism, but the claim remains a defensive statement rather than verified disclosure.","contrary_evidence":["The article does not independently verify the cost accounting she described."],"lenses":["7B.2","7B.6"]}

- Defense of reserve spending as public welfare.
  SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Hasina says Bangladesh parked part of its reserves in investments","publisher":"bdnews24.com","publication_date":"2022-11-14","url":"https://bdnews24.com/bangladesh/iihk2boscy","claim":"Hasina said the government had parked part of its reserves in investments or used the money for public welfare, denied that money was stolen, and framed the spending as serving the people.","locator":"L141-L156","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Direct contemporaneous report of Hasina’s public defense of reserve use, with specific figures and a clear quotation, but still a self-serving statement.","final_evidence_use":"context","period_fit":"Directly in 2022 and directly about a contested fiscal claim.","ruler_attribution":"This is Hasina speaking personally as prime minister, but the source does not independently prove the reserve accounting or the absence of misuse.","contrary_evidence":["IMF and World Bank reporting in 2022-2023 described reserve pressure and macroeconomic strain."],"lenses":["7B.2","7B.8","7B.10"]}

- Professional central-bank appointment.
  SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Bangladesh appoints Abdur Rouf Talukder as central bank governor","publisher":"bdnews24.com","publication_date":"2022-06-11","url":"https://bdnews24.com/bangladesh/bangladesh-appoints-abdur-rouf-talukder-as-central-bank-governor","claim":"The government appointed finance secretary Abdur Rouf Talukder, a long-serving civil servant with more than 18 years in the Finance Division and experience in budget reform and macroeconomic management, as Bangladesh Bank governor.","locator":"L141-L149","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Direct appointment report with detailed professional background and clear period fit.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly in 2022 and directly about appointment quality.","ruler_attribution":"Attributable to the Hasina government’s appointment choice, though the article does not prove Hasina personally screened the candidate.","contrary_evidence":["One technocratic appointment does not erase broader patronage or self-dealing concerns elsewhere in the record."],"lenses":["7B.5","7B.9"]}

- Public praise of housing for destitute people.
  SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"The biggest joy: PM breaks down in tears in parliament","publisher":"The Daily Star","publication_date":"2022-03-30","url":"https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/the-biggest-joy-pm-breaks-down-tears-parliament-2994126","claim":"Hasina told parliament that giving land and houses to destitute people was one of the biggest joys of her life and framed housing the homeless as a core purpose of rule.","locator":"search-result snippet / lead paragraph","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Direct contemporaneous report of a public statement, but the available access here is via snippet rather than a fully quoted archive page.","final_evidence_use":"context","period_fit":"Directly in 2022 and directly about her public self-presentation on welfare and ethical purpose.","ruler_attribution":"Strongly attributable to Hasina as a personal statement, though it remains self-presentation rather than independent evidence of conduct.","contrary_evidence":["Later plot-allocation evidence suggests the public welfare persona coexisted with private network benefit."],"lenses":["7B.10","7B.8"]}

- Secret family plot allocations in 2022.
  SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"HC forms panel to probe plots given to Hasina, family","publisher":"The Daily Star","publication_date":"2024-10-24","url":"https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/crime-justice/news/hc-forms-panel-probe-plots-given-hasina-family-3735351","claim":"A writ petition alleged that in 2022 Rajuk issued allocation letters for 10-katha Purbachal plots to Hasina and six family members, that the allocations were later marked top state secret, and that files were removed from the Rajuk records section and hidden elsewhere before some were returned.","locator":"L174-L190","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Specific documentary allegations and dated allocation letters are quoted, but the article reports a petition and official assertions rather than a final judgment.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Retrospective evidence about 2022 allocations and concealment relevant to the target period.","ruler_attribution":"Directly tied to Hasina because the alleged allocations were in her and her family members names, though legal culpability is not finally adjudicated in the article.","contrary_evidence":["This is a petition-stage report, not a verdict."],"lenses":["7B.3","7B.4","7B.6","7B.7","7B.9"]}

- Anti-corruption commission finding on those plot allocations.
  SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"ACC finds proof of abuse of power in plots for Hasina, family","publisher":"bdnews24.com","publication_date":"2025-01-09","url":"https://bdnews24.com/bangladesh/e270f941f3b3","claim":"The Anti-Corruption Commission said it had uncovered evidence of abuse of power in the allocation of 60 kathas of plots in Purbachal to Hasina and six family members, and said documents showed Hasina received a plot allocation letter dated August 3, 2022.","locator":"L141-L159 and L151-L155","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"The article quotes the ACC director general and cites reviewed documents with specific dates, but the investigation had not yet become a final court judgment in this piece.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Retrospective evidence about a 2022 act squarely relevant to the target year.","ruler_attribution":"Strongly attributable to Hasina and her close family because the documents name them and the alleged benefit is personal, though final legal resolution is pending in the article.","contrary_evidence":["Still an investigation report rather than a final adjudication."],"lenses":["7B.3","7B.4","7B.7","7B.9"]}

- Punishment of a journalist who reported corruption.
  SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Bangladeshi journalist Imran Hossain Titu investigated under Digital Security Act","publisher":"Committee to Protect Journalists","publication_date":"2022-08-23","url":"https://cpj.org/2022/08/bangladeshi-journalist-imran-hossain-titu-investigated-under-digital-security-act/","claim":"A journalist was investigated under the Digital Security Act after publishing a video investigation alleging corruption by a local shrine management committee, and he said politicians and their associates repeatedly threatened him and tried to stop publication.","locator":"L516-L527","source_type":"NGO","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"A detailed contemporaneous NGO case report with the journalist’s account, dates, and retaliation allegations, though the direct government nexus is still indirect.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly in 2022 and directly about retaliation against corruption reporting.","ruler_attribution":"Attributed to the governing environment under Hasina because the Digital Security Act and police process were used against a corruption reporter, but the immediate complainant was a local shrine-related actor rather than Hasina herself.","contrary_evidence":["The alleged corruption concerned a local shrine committee, so the personal nexus to Hasina is indirect."],"lenses":["7B.2","7B.6","7B.7"]}

- Systematic Digital Security Act pressure on critics of the prime minister.
  SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Bangladesh: Freedom on the Net 2022 Country Report","publisher":"Freedom House","publication_date":"2022","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-net/2022","claim":"Freedom House said the government increasingly used the Digital Security Act to harass, charge, and arrest people for online and offline speech, and that about 40 percent of cases were filed for slandering or making indecent comments about the prime minister or other influential people.","locator":"L419-L425 and L421-L424","source_type":"NGO","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Well-established rights report with quantitative claims and specific examples, though it remains country-level rather than a direct personal finding.","final_evidence_use":"context","period_fit":"Directly about the 2022 information environment and abuse of law to punish critics.","ruler_attribution":"Government-level pattern under Hasina's administration; it does not prove her personal instruction in each case, but it does directly connect to criticism of the prime minister.","contrary_evidence":["This is systematic country-level context, not a personal confession or direct order."],"lenses":["7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10"]}

- False honorific claim amplified by state media and a minister.
  SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"UN did not name Bangladesh PM as worlds second best prime minister","publisher":"AFP Fact Check","publication_date":"2022-10-16","url":"https://factcheck.afp.com/doc.afp.com.32LC2GA","claim":"AFP debunked a claim that the UN named Hasina the worlds second best prime minister and documented that the false claim was amplified by Bangladeshs state-run BSS and a government minister.","locator":"L60-L75 and L81-L83","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Independent fact-check with direct UN confirmation that the award did not exist and documentation of who amplified the falsehood.","final_evidence_use":"context","period_fit":"Directly in 2022 and directly about misleading public praise surrounding Hasina.","ruler_attribution":"Indirect but meaningful: the false claim was circulated by state media and a minister under Hasinas government, though not shown to have been authored by Hasina herself.","contrary_evidence":["The article does not show Hasina personally requested or repeated the false claim."],"lenses":["7B.1","7B.2","7B.10"]}

**Search and rejection summary**
I screened roughly 30 documents across UNB, Jago News, bdnews24, The Daily Star, CPJ, Freedom House, AFP, Reuters/Reuters-licensed reprints, and later ACC/court coverage.

Kept:
- Direct 2022 public statements on housing, reserves, transparency, and appointments.
- 2022-anchored and later-retrospective documents that quote dated 2022 plot allocation letters and official investigation language.
- One NGO case report on retaliation against a corruption journalist.
- One country-level rights report and one fact-check documenting propaganda-like false praise circulating around Hasina in 2022.

Rejected:
- Generic corruption indices and broad governance summaries that did not establish a Hasina-specific personal nexus.
- Repetitive coverage of the same housing and reserve claims when a better or more precise source was already retained.
- Out-of-period 2024-2026 articles that were not tied back to a 2022 act or statement.
- News items about repression, election pressure, or development policy that fit 3B/4B/5B/6B better than personal integrity unless they directly implicated concealment, favoritism, or punishment of scrutiny.
- Allegations without any documentary basis or with only generic country-level context.

**Remaining gaps**
- The biggest gap is direct first-person evidence of Hasina personally correcting a false claim or admitting a specific error in 2022.
- The plot-allocation evidence is strong on self-dealing and concealment, but less conclusive on the exact extent of Hasina’s personal direction versus senior officials acting on her behalf.
- More search would help on 2022 asset-disclosure records, procurement and licensing decisions, and any first-person responses to allegations of corruption or misuse of office.
- The current record supports a meaningful integrity dossier, but the personal-nexus boundary remains thinner than in the repression chapters.
